s1.syndrome_frame: subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: mild cough, sputum production, and rhinorrhea
cavitary and noncavitary nodules and masses with faint surrounding ground-glass opacity
fungal elements with yeast-like structures and septate hyphae
key_facts: 10-day history of hemoptysis
1-month history of mild cough, sputum production, and rhinorrhea
mild wheezing bilaterally on examination
elevated C-reactive protein level of 7 mg/dL
normal white-cell count with a neutrophil count of 3.97 × 10^3/μL
negative HIV testing
negative initial microbiologic studies
multiple nodules and masses in both lung fields on chest radiograph
cavitary lesions with thick, irregular walls and septa-like structures on chest CT
patent vessels within the lesions on coronal maximum intensity projection image
small bilateral pleural effusion
normal antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody titers
diffuse granulomatous inflammation on bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage and transbronchial biopsy
histopathologic analysis showing diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and fungal elements

per_call: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia with granulomatous reaction

shortlist.label: invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: presence of cavitary lesions with thick, irregular walls and septa-like structures, and histopathologic analysis showing diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and fungal elements

shortlist.label: histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: subacute pulmonary syndrome with hemoptysis and granulomatous inflammation, and presence of multiple nodules and masses in both lung fields

shortlist.label: blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation to invasive aspergillosis, with cavitary lesions and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: presence of granulomatous inflammation and possibility of fungal infection, although less likely given the negative initial microbiologic studies

shortlist.label: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: similar clinical presentation to invasive aspergillosis, with cavitary lesions and granulomatous inflammation, and possibility of chronic infection

raw.rationale: The presence of diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, fungal elements, and yeast-like structures associated with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching on histopathologic analysis are consistent with invasive aspergillosis. The clinical presentation of hemoptysis, cough, and sputum production, along with the radiographic findings of cavitary lesions and the 'halo sign' on chest CT, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: histoplasmosis
rejected.why: While histoplasmosis can cause granulomatous inflammation, the presence of septate hyphae with acute-angle branching is more characteristic of aspergillosis.

rejected.label: blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with broad-based budding yeast, which was not described in the histopathologic findings.

rejected.label: cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Cryptococcosis is more commonly associated with HIV infection or immunosuppression, which was not present in this patient, and the histopathologic findings did not describe the characteristic encapsulated yeast.

rejected.label: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
rejected.why: While chronic pulmonary aspergillosis can present with similar radiographic findings, the acute presentation and the presence of diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation are more consistent with invasive aspergillosis.
